html:
The palace of the sultans of Yogyakarta in central Java, Indonesia, built from 1755. It is still the home of the reigning sultan and a living centre of Javanese court culture.

The palace was founded after the Treaty of Giyanti of 1755 split the old Mataram Sultanate into two kingdoms, Surakarta and Yogyakarta, with the Dutch as referees. Prince Mangkubumi became the first sultan, Hamengkubuwono I, and laid out the palace on a line running north to Mount Merapi and south to the sea. Its courtyards and pavilions hold royal heirlooms, and its musicians and dancers keep alive gamelan music and court dance.

The prince Diponegoro, who led the Java War against the Dutch, was a son of the third sultan. In the Indonesian revolution, Sultan Hamengkubuwono IX backed the Republic, and Yogyakarta served as its capital from 1946 to 1949, after independence was declared. In return it became a special region, and its sultan is also its governor.
